paper_title: Spectroscopy as a test of Coulomb's law - A probe of the hidden sector
suggested_experiment_name: Atomic spectroscopy Coulomb's law test (hydrogen/hydrogenic/exotic atoms)
coupling_convention: kinetic mixing epsilon (=chi), dimensionless; emitted as actual value 10^(Log10 epsilon)
notes: Paper derives bounds on hidden photon kinetic mixing chi vs mass m_gamma' (keV to >MeV range) from tests of Coulomb's law using precision atomic spectroscopy (Lamb shift in H, He ions, combined 1s-2s/2s-8s transitions, plus speculative bounds from true muonium and muonic hydrogen). Coupling type is unambiguously DarkPhoton (kinetic mixing chi). However, all exclusion limits are presented only as curves in figures (Figs 1,3,4,5) with no tabulated numerical (mass, chi) pairs; the text gives energy-shift uncertainties (e.g. Delta M* ~ 2e-10 eV) but not readable data points. Rough estimate: best bound chi ~ 1e-5 near a few keV, but not reliably extractable, so data_points left empty. This is a laboratory/spectroscopy bound (not DM haloscope), so no DM density.
